summary: SELENIX is an interactive lunar mission-planning application designed to help users compare potential landing sites and mission dates near the Moon’s south pole. It visualizes the positions of the Sun and Earth relative to the local horizon to assess solar availability and potential direct-to-Earth communication opportunities. Its key feature, the Mission Window Finder, identifies periods when sunlight and Earth visibility overlap. details:
SELENIX is an interactive lunar mission-planning application developed to simplify the evaluation of potential landing sites near the Moon’s south pole. It allows users to select landing locations, customise mission dates and durations, and visualise the positions of the Sun and Earth relative to the lunar horizon through an interactive 3D model. Its key innovation, the Mission Window Finder, identifies periods when sunlight and geometric Earth visibility overlap, helping users explore potential opportunities for solar power generation and direct-to-Earth communication.

The project benefits mission planners, educators, students, and the public by presenting complex lunar conditions through an accessible interface. Its intended impact is to make preliminary lunar mission analysis easier to understand, compare, and explore.

SELENIX was developed using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, with Three.js for 3D visualisation. Deployed using netlify and used claude for debugging and coding assitance. The team considered usability, visual clarity, site selection, solar availability, Earth visibility, and transparency of scientific assumptions. Its creativity lies in combining these factors into one interactive platform, particularly through the Mission Window Finder. The application clearly identifies its analytical calculations, synthetic terrain data, and simplified models as demonstrations rather than validated mission predictions.
